title: Welcome to your workshop
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
01 / 16
Welcome to your workshop
A beginner guide to WZXU Garage Flow
1
1
Open the app
Visit the link at the bottom of this page. The
Dashboard is your starting point. Bookmark it in
the browser you will use for work.
2
2
Know what it does
Keep customers and vehicles together,
document work, prepare estimates and
invoices, and record payments.
3
3
Start with Settings
Set up your business first. Then follow pages
6-14 to practice one complete service visit.
Remember: All people, records and prices in this guide are fictional examples. The app is available online, but its records stay in the browser on your device.
Result: You know where to begin. Pages 2-5 introduce the app and set your defaults.

title: Find your way around
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
02 / 16
Find your way around
Use the Dashboard as your daily starting point.
1
1
Use the left navigation
Open Jobs, Customers, Vehicles, Estimates or
Invoices. Service history shows work by
vehicle.
2
2
Read the totals
Review jobs this month, payments received this
month and outstanding balance. These
describe records saved in this browser.
3
3
Search or start new work
Search by name, phone, VIN, plate or invoice.
Use + New Customer for a first-time visitor, or +
New Job for the next service.
Remember: Supplier links open external websites. They are reference links, not a parts-ordering or automatic pricing system.
Result: You can navigate to records and recognize the main dashboard controls.

title: Set up your business
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
03 / 16
Set up your business
Settings > Business and branding
1
1
Enter business details
Fill Business name, Owner, Phone, Email,
Website and Business address as needed.
These details identify your business on
documents.
2
2
Choose app branding
App name controls the app label. Scroll down to
Business logo to choose a PNG, JPEG or
WebP up to 2 MB, or keep the default logo.
3
Save the settings
Scroll to the bottom and click Save settings.
Wait for Settings saved. A draft message alone
does not apply your changes.
Remember: This example uses WZXU Demo Workshop only for training. Enter your actual business details in your own app.
Result: Your saved business identity is used for the app and customer documents.

title: Choose billing defaults
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
04 / 16
Choose billing defaults
Settings > Billing defaults
1
1
Choose currency and labor
Expand Billing defaults. Select Currency and
enter Default hourly labor rate. Our guide keeps
USD and a $100 hourly default.
2
2
Review tax and numbering
Set Tax rate (%) and your Job, Estimate and
Invoice prefixes. Our example uses 0% tax with
JOB, EST and INV.
3
Apply the defaults
Scroll down and click Save settings. You can
also edit the disclaimer and document footer
text in this section.
Remember: Tax applies to parts, labor and fees after discount. Changing currency changes the label; it does not convert existing amounts. Example tax is not tax advice.
Result: New documents start from your saved defaults; always review each document before issuing it.

title: Prepare repeat services
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
05 / 16
Prepare repeat services
Settings > Services and Inspection template
1
1
Name your services
Expand Services. Edit names or use Add
service at the bottom. Up and Down change the
display order.
2
2
Set example prices
For Oil + Filter, this guide uses Parts price $45
and Labor price $35. These become the
example $80 service.
3
Save your reusable setup
Review Inspection template below the services
list, then click Save settings. Quick services will
use the saved service defaults.
Remember: Prices shown here are teaching examples, not recommended rates. Business Reference prices are separate notes and do not automatically price a job.
Result: You have a repeatable Oil + Filter service ready for the job editor.

title: Add your first customer
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
06 / 16
Add your first customer
Dashboard > + New Customer
1
1
Enter the customer name
The New job flow opens at Customer. Enter
Customer name * and any useful contact
details.
2
2
Keep useful notes
Add Customer notes when needed. This
example is Alex Martinez (DEMO), a fictional
training customer.
3
3
Save, then continue
Click Save customer locally. After confirmation,
click Next to continue to Vehicle. To stop here,
use Close & keep draft.
Remember: You can also review and edit saved customer records from Customers in the left navigation. Check for an existing customer before adding a duplicate.
Result: Alex is saved and selected for this service visit.

title: Link the customer vehicle
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
07 / 16
Link the customer vehicle
New job > Vehicle > Add a vehicle
1
1
Confirm the owner
Keep the saved customer selected. Enter Year,
Make * and Model *. Our example is a 2020
Honda Civic.
2
2
Record vehicle details
Enter Mileage and any known VIN, plate,
engine, trim or color. We use 42000 miles and
leave identifying fields blank.
3
3
Save the vehicle
Click Save vehicle locally, then Next. Existing
vehicle / skip lets you select an existing vehicle
or continue without one.
Remember: The form scrolls. Year and customer selection are above the visible area in this screenshot. Saved vehicles can also be reviewed from Vehicles.
Result: The Honda Civic is linked to Alex and selected for the service visit.

title: Follow the three job steps
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
08 / 16
Follow the three job steps
Customer > Vehicle > Work & billing
1
1
Reuse saved records
For a returning visit, start with + New Job and
choose Existing customer. Select the correct
customer before continuing.
2
2
Select the right vehicle
At Vehicle, choose the customer vehicle.
Confirm the Honda Civic appears before
clicking Next.
3
3
Continue to work details
Click Next for Work & billing. Select Document
type: Estimate for a quote, Invoice for billing, or
Work order for a job record.
Remember: We continue the same flow started on page 6; do not create a second customer or vehicle. Back returns to an earlier step.
Result: The correct customer and vehicle are attached before prices and work details are entered.

title: Price the service
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
09 / 16
Price the service
Work & billing > Quick services, Parts and Labor
1
Add the service once
Choose Estimate and work status Estimate
above this view. Click Oil + Filter under Quick
services to add our saved service.
2
2
Check the parts line
Confirm Part name, Quantity and Customer unit
price. Our line is quantity 1 at $45. Unit cost
(internal) is a separate field.
3
3
Check labor and totals
Below Parts, review Labor pricing and Flat labor
amount ($35). Scroll down to Totals: $45 + $35
= $80, with zero fees, discount and tax.
Remember: Add part and Add labor create extra lines. Review the total after every change; do not click the same quick service repeatedly by mistake.
Result: The example estimate totals $80.00 before any payment.

title: Document the work
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
10 / 16
Document the work
Work & billing > Inspection and recommendations
1
1
Add inspection details
Expand Inspection (optional). Use Add
inspection checklist or Add inspection item if
needed, and record your findings.
2
2
Write useful follow-up notes
Add Inspection notes, Recommendations and
Next service recommendation. Technician
notes are higher in the same form.
3
3
Keep a draft or finalize
For this exercise, click Close & keep draft.
When the record is ready to finalize, click Save
locally instead.
Remember: Only document findings you actually observed. Our notes are marked DEMO; they are not a diagnosis or completed inspection.
Result: Work details stay with the service record and can appear on its customer document.

title: Resume and finalize a draft
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
11 / 16
Resume and finalize a draft
Dashboard > Continue a saved draft
1
1
Recognize draft status
Draft saved locally protects unfinished work. It
is different from saving a finalized job, estimate
or invoice.
2
2
Resume your work
Click Resume draft next to Alex. The app
returns to the saved step with the customer,
vehicle and $80 service intact.
3
Finalize the estimate
Review the details and scroll to Save locally.
The document preview opens as Estimate
EST-0001.
Remember: Close & keep draft preserves unfinished work. Discard draft removes that unfinished draft; it is not the normal Save button.
Result: The estimate is saved as a record and available for review.

title: Turn an estimate into an invoice
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
12 / 16
Turn an estimate into an invoice
Saved estimate > Convert to invoice
1
1
Review before converting
Check Estimate EST-0001, the customer,
vehicle, service and $80 total. Scroll down to
review all document details.
2
2
Convert after approval
When the customer has approved the work,
click Convert to invoice. Conversion updates
the saved document.
3
Check the result
Our document becomes INV-0001 with work
status Approved and a reference to EST-0001.
Its balance is $80 until payment is recorded.
Remember: An estimate is a proposed price; an invoice records billing. Conversion does not email the customer, collect approval, or charge a payment.
Result: The invoice retains the customer, vehicle, service lines and estimate reference.

title: Record a received payment
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
13 / 16
Record a received payment
Invoice > Edit / record payment
1
1
Open payment entry
Click Edit / record payment on the invoice, then
scroll to Payments and click Add payment.
Review the suggested amount.
2
2
Enter the payment details
Review Payment date, Amount paid and
Payment method. We record $80 as Other with
a DEMO note; no money changes hands.
3
3
Save and verify balance
Set work status Completed when appropriate,
then click Save locally at the bottom. The
invoice shows Paid and balance due $0.00.
Remember: This records a payment received elsewhere; it does not process a card or transfer money. A smaller payment leaves a remaining balance.
Result: INV-0001 totals $80, payments total $80, and the balance is $0.

title: Download or print a document
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
14 / 16
Download or print a document
Open an invoice or estimate preview.
1
1
Download the PDF
Click Download PDF for a local file. Open the
downloaded file and check the business details
and document number before sharing.
2
2
Choose a print style
Keep Low-ink print checked for black text on
white. Uncheck it for the branded version with
your logo.
3
3
Print when needed
Click Print / Save as PDF to use the browser
print dialog. Turn off Headers and footers there
if you do not want the browser URL.
Remember: Send the saved file through your preferred email or messaging app. Garage Flow does not send it automatically. Our verified download is INV-0001.
Result: You have a customer-ready document saved outside the app.

title: Find a previous service
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
15 / 16
Find a previous service
Service history, search and reference tools
1
1
Filter the vehicle history
Open Service history and choose a vehicle in
Vehicle history. Our Civic shows its mileage,
service and recommendations.
2
2
Reopen the document
Click INV-0001 to open the saved invoice.
Customers and Vehicles also let you review
their linked records.
3
3
Search across records
Use Search all records at the top to find names,
phone numbers, VINs, plates or document
numbers.
Remember: Business Reference stores owner reference notes and service prices; it does not set job prices. Supplier links on the Dashboard open external sites.
Result: You can trace a vehicle visit back to the saved invoice and its work details.

title: Back up and restore safely
text:
WZXU GARAGE FLOW  /  BEGINNER GUIDE
16 / 16
Back up and restore safely
Backup / Restore > Export ALL JSON
1
1
Export your records
Click Export ALL JSON. Keep the downloaded
JSON somewhere safe outside this browser.
Repeat after important changes.
2
2
Preview before restoring
Choose a Backup JSON file and review Backup
preview. Replace current data replaces
records, settings and drafts; Cancel leaves
them alone.
3
3
Know the other tools
Preview previous version reviews one local
recovery copy. Add demo data creates
samples. Factory reset removes local records
and recovery.
Remember: No automatic cloud sync: another browser, device or domain has separate data. Back up before moving. Demo totals affect reports. Factory reset is destructive.
Result: Export regularly. Restore only after checking the preview and saving any current data you need.
